From: Anna Patel <anna@gamma.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sizing question for reserved capacity

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the call earlier. As promised I'm attaching a CSV with a one-week sample of production requests (timestamps but anonymized IDs). High level: daytime bursty traffic with two main endpoints (chat + embeddings). Typical context lengths vary: average 1.2k tokens for chat history (90th pct ~3k), embeddings requests are short. Concurrent chat model connections range 80–120 at peak; total QPS across endpoints peaks ~85 requests/sec and averages ~30 r/s.

A few asks from procurement up front: 1) a committed GPU pool recommendation that meets 95th percentile latency SLOs for chat (<= 600ms p95 for 2k context), 2) a pricing/discount schedule for a 12-month reserved commit with quarterly billing, and 3) what margin of headroom you recommend for sustainable autoscaling/burst.

Attached: gamma_workload_samples.csv

Best,
Anna
Head of Platform, Gamma AI

Anna — thanks for the telemetry; that helps a lot. We're reviewing the sample now. Quick clarifying Qs before we size:

- Which chat model variant do you expect to run in the pool (e.g., 70B quantized vs 13B)?
- Are embeddings and chat required on the same pool or can embeddings be routed to a lower-cost pool?
- Do you need live failover to a hosted fallback model during maintenance windows?

I'll loop in Ben (capacity economics) and Marissa (SLA/rollout) to give you a recommended GPU pool layout, headroom guidance, and a tiered commercial for a 12-month reserved commit. Expect a short proposal by EOD Friday.

Cheers,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Gamma AI workload — initial sizing calc

Folks — I ran the sample through our throughput model. Notes and attachments: redwood_pool_pricing_v2.xlsx (tabbed: workload assumptions, GPU-pool-layouts, pricing tiers). Key assumptions inline.

On assumptions:
- Chat model: planning for a 13B quantized variant (mixed int8/4), per-token exec is ~0.9x of our reference LLM; we used conservative 1.0x for headroom.
- Avg chat context: 1.2k tokens; 90th pct 3k — we modeled both.
- Request breakdown: chat 65% of cost/CPU; embeddings 35% and routed to a cheaper T4-equivalent worker pool unless Gamma requires same pool.

Sizing outcomes (target: p95 latency <= 600ms for chat at 95th percentile load):
- Minimal baseline pool (no headroom): 4x A100-80GB equiv GPUs — meets avg load but will exceed p95 during peaks.
- Recommended committed pool (12-mo, with 20% headroom): 6x A100-80GB equiv GPUs — supports 95 r/s sustained with concurrency targets and keeps p95 ~520ms.
- Conservative pool (for growth to 150 r/s + canary enabling): 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs.

Commercials (summary, see sheet for tiered pricing):
- List price (monthly) for 6x pool: $98,000/mo; with 12-mo reserved commit we can offer a 22% committed discount -> $76,440/mo.
- If Gamma signs an end-of-quarter commitment and pays annually upfront we can increase to a 28% discount ($70,560/mo equivalent).
- 8x pool list: $130k/mo; committed price (12-mo) 24% discount -> $98,800/mo.

Optional add-ons:
- Canary throughput guarantee: +$2,500/mo to reserve a hot standby capacity slice for rollouts (reduces cold-start variance).
- Extended support SLA (99.9% uptime SLA + 15-minute paging): +$6,500/mo.

I'm attaching the workbook for the math. If embeddings must run in the same pool, add ~1.5 GPUs to the 6x config for memory/IO headroom.

Ben
Principal Capacity Strategist, Redwood Inference

Anna — adding a few operational items so procurement has everything it needs when reviewing the SOW: 

- SLA targets: we will propose 99.5% baseline with optional upgrade to 99.9% (pricing noted above). We include automatic model fallback policies (can be restricted by you).
- Rollout canaries: we recommend enabling a 5% traffic canary in the same pool for the first 4 weeks of each major model change; we can reserve that as the small paid add-on Ben called out.
- Maintenance windows & planned capacity changes: commit contract includes one planned maintenance window per quarter; additional scheduled capacity changes can be requested with 7 days notice.
- Audit & compliance: SOC2 evidence and logging export included; we will provide an isolated VPC option for an additional one-time setup fee.

Next steps: Ben to confirm final numbers in the workbook; Dylan to capture revised commercial terms in the draft SOW and send to Anna/procurement with a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marissa
